current_activity: Chill sets up straggler rallying points along the Albert Canal and forms his battle group
notes: Event date: by nightfall of 4 September 1944 (MacDonald, ch. 6). Event definition: Postponing his withdrawal to the Rhineland, Chill sets up straggler rallying points along the Albert Canal and by nightfall of 4 September has collected Navy, Luftwaffe and military government troops (MacDonald, ch. 6). Event support: one source family (the US Army official history (CMH)). MacDonald, The Siegfried Line Campaign, ch. 6, p. 124: "he postponed his withdrawal in order to set up straggler rallying points along the canal". Location: Albert Canal; Beringen used as a representative point (inferred value) with a precision of 25 km. Location support: MacDonald names the Albert Canal only. Commander: Generalleutnant Kurt Chill (MacDonald, ch. 6).

current_activity: committed along the Meuse-Escaut Canal against the British ground advance of Market Garden
notes: Event date: 17 September 1944 (MacDonald, ch. 7). Event definition: Already committed along the Meuse-Escaut, Kampfgruppe Chill is to oppose the British ground troops (MacDonald, ch. 7). Event support: one source family (the US Army official history (CMH)). MacDonald, The Siegfried Line Campaign, ch. 7, p. 142: "Already committed along the Meuse-Escaut, Kampfgruppe Chill was to oppose the British ground troops". Location: Meuse-Escaut Canal; Neerpelt used as a representative point (inferred value) with a precision of 10 km. Location support: MacDonald names the Meuse-Escaut Canal only. Commander: Generalleutnant Kurt Chill (MacDonald, ch. 6). Opponents: British XXX Corps.

current_activity: part of the battle group committed with the 6th Parachute Regiment at Woensdrecht
notes: Event date: October 1944, before Woensdrecht fell on 16 October (MacDonald, ch. 9); 10 October is used (inferred value). Event definition: At Woensdrecht the Germans commit von der Heydte's 6th Parachute Regiment and a part of Kampfgruppe Chill; Woensdrecht falls on 16 October (MacDonald, ch. 9). Event support: one source family (the US Army official history (CMH)). MacDonald, The Siegfried Line Campaign, ch. 9, p. 221: "At Woensdrecht they committed both Colonel von der Heydte". Location: Woensdrecht, Noord-Brabant with a precision of 3 km. Location support: MacDonald names Woensdrecht. Commander: Generalleutnant Kurt Chill (MacDonald, ch. 6). Opponents: Canadian 2nd Infantry Division.
